top_choice_rationale: P001 (Katori and Ye, optical lattice clocks) rests on a distinct, separable idea: the magic-wavelength lattice cancels the light shift while holding very many atoms free of Doppler and recoil broadening, which neither laser cooling, the frequency comb nor ion clocks supply. The result is measured, near 1e-18, reproduced across independent laboratories and already used in tests of constant variation, dark-matter searches and relativistic geodesy. The two-name allocation is the cleanest on the shortlist, and the citation should be kept narrow to magic-wavelength lattice clocks. P002 (IceCube, Halzen and Karle) is the stronger discovery in the abstract, since it opens a new messenger, and the diffuse flux is secure, but crediting two names from a collaboration of hundreds with AMANDA and Baikal precursors and Yoshida omitted is discretionary, so I rank it second. An award is better than no award given two mature, defensible proposals, so P000 is last.
